_readme: This file controls the example scripts the dashboard generates for Flightsheets, Overclocking, and Watchdog (the 'New' button / auto-generated raw content). Edit the values/templates below to change what gets generated - no app.js edit or redeploy needed. The dashboard re-fetches this file on every page load.

%Placeholder% tokens inside a *_template string get replaced with live values from the dashboard form fields when the script is generated. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, including the % on both sides - a typo'd placeholder name will not be replaced and will show up literally in the generated script instead.
flightsheet.cpu_template / flightsheet.gpu_template / flightsheet.aux_template have exactly ONE placeholder: %RIG_GPU_JSON%.

It gets filled with the rig-gpu.json body (pretty-printed JSON, matching the rig-side generate_rig_gpu_json_from_conf()/convert-conf-to-rig-gpu-json.sh output) built by buildRigGpuJsonBody() in app.js from the Flightsheet form fields - custom vs. built-in miner, splitting POOL into url+pool_ssl, etc. need real branching logic, not just a field substitution, so that part isn't editable from this file the way the wrapper text (the tee target path, the systemctl service name) still is.

overclocking is split into 3 separate fields that get concatenated per-algorithm row into one generated script - apply_script_header (written once, before any rows), apply_script_algo_block (repeated once per algorithm row, joined together), and apply_script_footer (written once, after all rows):

apply_script_algo_block placeholders: %ALGO% (the case-pattern label, from the row's Algorithm field), %Lock Core Clock% %Core Clock Offset% %Lock Memory Clock% %Memory Clock Offset% %Power Limit% %Fan Mode% %Fan Value% - direct field values. Fan Mode is literally 'percent' or 'curve'; Fan Value is either the fan percent number or the curve string ('30:30,40:45,50:65') depending on Fan Mode.

apply_script_footer has no placeholders left - it's fully static. When FAN_MODE is 'curve' it updates the already-installed fan-curve.service's --curve value in place via sed and only restarts the daemon if that value actually changed, instead of rewriting/restarting the whole service on every miner (re)start. fan-curve.service itself (the systemd unit, fan_curve.py) is installed ONCE, separately, via Fan-control/py-nvtool/install_fan-curve.sh - it is intentionally NOT generated from this file, since it should not be recreated/bounced on every OC apply.

watchdog.conf_dir / watchdog.conf_path are plain values (not templates with placeholders) - the directory watchdog config gets mkdir'd into, and the full path the watchdog conf file gets written to/read from on each worker.

agentconf.conf_dir / agentconf.conf_path / agentconf.restart_command are the same kind of plain values, for the Settings modal's Agent Conf tab - the directory/path rigcontrol-agent.conf gets mkdir'd/written/read at on each worker, and the command run afterward when 'Restart agent after apply' is checked.

flightsheet_derivation holds the lookup tables the Flightsheets pool-short-name / coin-ticker auto-fill uses (deriveCoinForClipboard()/derivePoolSlugForClipboard() in app.js). It only ever fills in a blank 'pool' or 'coin' field - it never overwrites a value that's already present. Each key here is a FULL replacement if you edit it - copy the existing entries too, not just the new one, or you'll lose the built-in mappings.
algo_to_coin: {algo: COIN} - exact, case-insensitive match on the miner's algo field. Checked first, before the pool address is even looked at.

pool_coin_hints: [[substring, COIN], ...] - checked in order against the pool hostname if algo_to_coin had no match. First substring found in the hostname wins, so put more specific hints earlier if two could both match.
ambiguous_algo_defaults: {algo: null} - algos deliberately mapped to null (e.g. rx/0, kawpow are mined for many different coins) so the auto-fill leaves 'coin' blank instead of guessing wrong.

pool_slug_overrides: {derived_label: real_slug} - the pool short-name is normally just pulled from the pool hostname (e.g. 'herominers' from ca.pearl.herominers.com); this remaps specific derived labels to a nicer/more correct value.

known_miners holds the pool/algo flag layout for each known (built-in) miner - buildKnownMinerCommand() in app.js uses these to build the FULL command line (miner_config/root-level miner_command) at Flightsheet Save time; rig-side just substitutes %WALLET%/%PASS% and runs it, no per-miner flag logic left there. Unlike flightsheet_derivation above, each miner name here is its OWN top-level key, so you only need to include the miner(s) you're actually changing or adding here - any miner you don't list keeps its built-in default.
algo_flag: the flag placed before the algo value, e.g. "-a" -> "-a kawpow".

url_mode: "bare" (scheme stripped, e.g. "pool.example.com:3333") or "full" (scheme kept exactly as stored in pool_urls, e.g. "stratum+ssl://pool.example.com:3333") - depends on whether that miner's CLI accepts an inline stratum+tcp/ssl:// scheme on its pool flag.

pool_join: "repeat" (pool_template repeated once per pool_urls entry, space-joined - most miners, for failover pool support) or "comma"/"space" (pool_template used ONCE, with %POOL% filled by every pool address joined with that separator into a single flag value).

pool_template: the flag(s) for one pool entry (repeat mode) or the whole pool flag (comma/space mode) - %POOL% is replaced with the real address (or the joined list). %WALLET%/%PASS% must be left exactly as written (literal, including the % on both sides) - only the rig can resolve those, at launch time.
suffix_template (optional): appended once at the very end, after all pool_template repetitions - for miners whose wallet/pass flag isn't part of the per-pool repeat (e.g. rigel, gminer).

conditional_flag (optional): a TLS/SSL flag inserted as a PREFIX, only if `detect` isn't already found in the user's own extra args (so a manually-typed flag is never duplicated). when_true/when_false pick the value based on pool_ssl or the flightsheet's TLS checkbox.

flightsheet.cpu_template:
tee /etc/rigcontrol/rig-cpu.json > /dev/null <<'EOF'
%RIG_GPU_JSON%
EOF
sudo systemctl restart docker_events_cpu
flightsheet.gpu_template:
tee /etc/rigcontrol/rig-gpu.json > /dev/null <<'EOF'
%RIG_GPU_JSON%
EOF
sudo systemctl restart docker_events_gpu
flightsheet.aux_template:
tee /etc/rigcontrol/rig-aux.json > /dev/null <<'EOF'
%RIG_GPU_JSON%
EOF
sudo systemctl restart docker_events_aux

overclocking.apply_script_header:
tee /usr/local/bin/gpu_apply_ocs.sh > /dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# gpu_apply_ocs.sh <algo_name> / <custom miner name>
# Generated from the dashboard's Overclock module - edit there, not by hand.
# Note: a row's Algorithm field can list multiple comma-separated algo names
# (e.g. keryxhash,keryx-miner,keryx-minerx) - they're combined into one case
# pattern below, joined by '|', so they all share this row's OC settings.

ALGO="${1:-}"
if [[ -z "$ALGO" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <algo_name>"
    exit 1
fi

ALGO_LOWER=$(echo "$ALGO" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

case "$ALGO_LOWER" in
overclocking.apply_script_algo_block:
%ALGO%)
        CORE=%Lock Core Clock%
        CORE_OFFSET=%Core Clock Offset%
        MEM=%Lock Memory Clock%
        MEM_OFFSET=%Memory Clock Offset%
        POWER_LIMIT=%Power Limit%
        FAN_MODE="%Fan Mode%"
        FAN_VALUE="%Fan Value%"
        ;;
overclocking.apply_script_footer:
*)
        echo "No OC profile defined for algo '$ALGO' - add a row for it in the dashboard's Overclock module"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

echo "Setting GPU OC for algo '$ALGO': core=$CORE (+$CORE_OFFSET) mem=$MEM (+$MEM_OFFSET) power_limit=$POWER_LIMIT fan=$FAN_MODE:$FAN_VALUE"
CMD=(py-nvtool --setcore "$CORE" --setcoreoffset "$CORE_OFFSET" --setmem "$MEM" --setmemoffset "$MEM_OFFSET")
if [[ -n "$POWER_LIMIT" && "$POWER_LIMIT" != "0" ]]; then
    CMD+=(--setpl "$POWER_LIMIT")
fi
if [[ "$FAN_MODE" == "percent" ]]; then
    CMD+=(--setfan "$FAN_VALUE")
fi
"${CMD[@]}"

# fan-curve.service is installed ONCE, separately (Fan-control/py-nvtool/install_fan-curve.sh) -
# this only ever updates its --curve value in place, and only restarts the already-running daemon
# when that value actually changed, instead of rewriting/bouncing the whole service on every single
# miner (re)start regardless of whether the curve differs from before.
if [[ "$FAN_MODE" == "curve" ]]; then
    FAN_SVC=/etc/systemd/system/fan-curve.service
    if [[ -f "$FAN_SVC" ]]; then
        CURRENT_CURVE=$(sed -n 's/.*--curve "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$FAN_SVC")
        if [[ "$CURRENT_CURVE" != "$FAN_VALUE" ]]; then
            echo "Fan curve changed - updating fan-curve.service and restarting it..."
            sed -i "s|--curve \"[^\"]*\"|--curve \"$FAN_VALUE\"|" "$FAN_SVC"
            systemctl daemon-reload
            systemctl restart fan-curve.service
        fi
    else
        echo "WARNING: fan-curve.service is not installed - run Fan-control/py-nvtool/install_fan-curve.sh once to set it up, then re-apply OC"
    fi
fi
EOF
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/gpu_apply_ocs.sh
